assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Response provides discount tier table, passenger type table, and zones table, but NO dedicated rolling window counting table with boundary testing (30 days included/excluded).

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note.
assertions.evidence: Child rows show '20%' discount regardless of ticket count: 'Child — flat discount, no travel history | Child | 0 | 20%' and 'Child — flat discount regardless of travel | Child | {4, 20, 40} | 20%'

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: Tier table shows 0%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 40% discounts at counts 0, 5, 10, 20, 40. Max 40% shown: 'At maximum tier | 40 | 40%'

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: No rolling window boundary test table present. Response acknowledges 'Rolling window edge: If exactly 30 days ago you bought 3 tickets, are they included or excluded?' as unresolved open question.

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: Only one value set appears: 'Child — flat discount regardless | Child | {4, 20, 40} | 20%'. Discount tier table uses individual counts (5, 7, 9, 10, 20, 40), not value sets per tier.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier (e.g. {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} or {5, 9} for min/max → 5%) — not one row per boundary value.
assertions.evidence: Tier table uses individual rows: 'At first discount threshold | 5 | 5%' and 'Mid first tier | 7 | 5%' and 'Top of first tier | 9 | 5%' — three separate rows instead of one row with value set {5..9}.

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: Tier mapping appears in both 'Reis Discount Tier' table and 'Discount by Passenger Type' table (Adult rows at 4→5%, 40→40%), creating duplication.

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: Response contains markdown tables only. No @TableTest methods or @DisplayName annotations present in the output.

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the class or the tier method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express.
assertions.evidence: Response contains no @Description annotations. Open questions section describes ambiguities but is not part of annotation metadata.

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: No annotations present in response — only markdown tables.

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description is absent, so this passes by the 'Passes if @Description is absent' rule.

assertions.text: The eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (or equivalent) with a value set to show that the discount applies regardless of zone.
assertions.evidence: Dedicated 'Zones Do Not Affect Discount' table shows Adult with zones {1 zone, 3 zones} both receiving 5% discount, demonstrating zone-irrelevance.

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR} (or equivalent) in at least one row of the eligibility table.
assertions.evidence: Adult and Senior listed as separate rows: 'Adult — no travel history yet | Adult | 0 | 0%' and 'Senior — same ladder as adult | Senior | 4 | 5%' — not combined in a value set.
Tier table shows only: 0%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 40%. Missing: 15%, 25%, 30%, 35% tiers.

assertions.text: Each tier in the discount ladder is expressed as a single row with a value set for ticket counts — not split across multiple rows.
assertions.evidence: 5% tier split across three rows: 'At first discount threshold | 5 | 5%', 'Mid first tier | 7 | 5%', 'Top of first tier | 9 | 5%'.

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively (e.g. '14 days ago', '30 days ago') rather than using absolute dates.
assertions.evidence: No rolling window table present in response.

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table.
assertions.evidence: Three tables provided: 'Reis Discount Tier', 'Discount by Passenger Type', and 'Zones Do Not Affect Discount' — each addressing separate concerns.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations.
assertions.evidence: Discount by Passenger Type table includes 3 Adult rows (0, 4, 40) and 3 Child rows, duplicating tier mapping already in Reis Discount Tier table.
